A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FedComLoc work. Their text, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable, and retained material can be matched despite substantial reformatting and renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original FedMNIST and FedCIFAR10 experiments, including accuracy, convergence, communication comparisons and compression ablations in Section 4 and Appendix B.

after.justification: V2 retains those experiments and adds original FEMNIST and Shakespeare results in Section 4.8 and compression timing measurements in Appendix C.5.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 retains the same updates, control variates and three compression placements. Section 3.2 expands their explanation without establishing a changed procedure. Combined sparsification and quantization already appeared in v1 Appendix B.3.

E1.justification: V2 adds FEMNIST handwriting classification with writer-based clients and Shakespeare next-character prediction with role-based clients. These extend the original FedMNIST/FedCIFAR10 coverage to naturally partitioned populations and a language task.

E2.justification: The existing comparisons retain FedAvg, sparseFedAvg and Scaffold; the added benchmarks reuse existing comparators. FedProx, FedDyn, FedNova and sign-based methods receive discussion but no newly reported evaluated comparisons.

E3.justification: The added benchmarks introduce study-specific settings: 3,000 communication rounds, 10 sampled clients per round, a FEMNIST CNN and a two-layer, 256-unit Shakespeare LSTM. V2 also adds rounds-to-target-accuracy evaluation and controlled local-update timing. Settings for the retained MNIST/CIFAR10 experiments are unchanged; the new study's description of p as a participation rate is ambiguous.

E4.justification: Appendix C.5 adds a supplementary analysis of compression overhead, comparing uncompressed, TopK and quantized local-update times across four models. Existing sparsity, heterogeneity, local-iteration, variant and double-compression ablations are retained. Appendix C.4 mainly interprets existing convergence plots.

E5.justification: Appendix C.5 newly states that timing measurements are averaged over 10 runs. V1 contains no corresponding run-count disclosure. This does not establish increased repetitions or new uncertainty reporting for the retained accuracy experiments.

E6.justification: Original numerical tables and plotted results are retained. New Table 3 reports FedComLoc-Com accuracy of 82.31%/51.56% on FEMNIST/Shakespeare versus SparseFedAvg's 78.14%/43.55%, while dense FedAvg remains higher at 86.63%/56.29%. Table 4 adds 84.7%/77.1% reductions in rounds to specified targets, and Table 5 adds measured compression overhead below 2%.

T1.justification: The optimization objective, compressor definitions and mathematical updates are unchanged. Despite their headings, Section 5.1 and Appendix C.4 introduce neither convergence theorems nor proofs: they discuss missing guarantees and empirical convergence.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the same central contributions: combining Scaffnew with compression, introducing three variants and reducing communication in heterogeneous federated learning. The revised conclusion preserves that central claim; the additional experiments expand its supporting evidence.

C2.justification: V2 substantially expands interpretation and limitations. Section 5 explicitly acknowledges missing guarantees even for convex objectives, distinguishes GPU timing from edge-device latency and energy costs, and explains restricted baseline coverage. Broader Impact adds the specific risk that biased compression underrepresents minority or rare client data.

D1.justification: V2 adds FedJAX preprocessing references, new-model specifications, partial-sorting and vectorized-compression implementation descriptions, and A100 40GB timing details. Existing software versions and the promised future code release remain unchanged. Figure 1 loses the explanation that Table 1 accuracies are maxima after hyperparameter tuning.

R1.justification: New Appendix A discusses SignSGD, momentum-based sign methods and variance-reduced sign methods, citing Bernstein, Sun and Jiang. FEMNIST and FedJAX references are also added, and Section 5.5 positions additional FL frameworks as complementary. The main positioning relative to Scaffnew remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Editorial changes concentrate in the expanded variant explanations and rewritten closing material, now separated into Discussion, Conclusion and Broader Impact. V2 also adds a contents list and related-work appendix. Most existing introduction, related-work and experimental prose remains substantially unchanged.

P2.justification: The paper changes from a two-column main text to a single-column journal layout, with redesigned front matter and widespread resizing and relocation of displays. Tables 3–5 are added while original plots are retained. Figure 1 gains misleading '100% Top-K' and '30% Top-K' subplot labels although both columns show multiple ratios.

improvement.justification: The naturally partitioned handwriting and language benchmarks in Tables 3–4 substantially address v1's limited practical validation, while Table 5 adds measured computational overhead. Explicit theoretical, hardware and fairness limitations improve transparency. Ambiguous participation wording and misleading Figure 1 labels weaken reporting, but these localized problems do not outweigh the substantial gains in empirical coverage and qualification.
